name: Sterling-Nakamura Holographic Decoy Projector HDP-3 'Mirage'
description: While not a weapon itself, the HDP-3 is classified as tactical ordnance because of its role in combat operations. The device projects a convincing holographic image of a human figure — complete with simulated thermal signature, acoustic footstep generation, and movement patterns derived from motion-capture libraries — that can draw fire, trigger automated defenses, and deceive security systems. The hologram is projected from a small emitter that can be thrown, placed, or drone-delivered, and the projected figure walks, runs, or takes cover according to pre-programmed behavioral scripts. Against human observers, the deception fails at distances under 5 meters. Against automated systems, it is convincing at any range that the sensors can detect it.
specifications:
projector size: 8 cm diameter disc
projection range: Up to 20 meters from emitter
hologram fidelity: Convincing beyond 5 meters to human observers
thermal simulation: Embedded IR emitter mimics body heat
acoustic simulation: Speaker generates footstep and movement sounds
behavioral scripts: Walk, run, take cover, fire weapon (visual only)
battery life: 10 minutes of projection
weight: 0.15 kg
deployment: Hand-thrown, placed, or drone-delivered
story_hooks: A witness swears they saw a person flee a crime scene, but security footage shows a holographic projection from an HDP-3 emitter found on the roof — someone used a decoy to create a false witness sighting.
An HDP-3 was used to trigger a SAT-2 autonomous turret into expending its ammunition on a hologram, allowing the real attackers to walk through the now-empty defense perimeter.
related_entities: Vespid Dynamics Shrike Autonomous Turret SAT-2

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact disc-shaped tactical emitter with a low-profile industrial design. The top surface features a subtle lens array arranged in a concentric pattern around a central optic dome. Minimal external controls, designed for rapid deployment and concealment.
physical_description.dimensions: 8 cm diameter × 3.2 cm height. Lens array spans 6 cm across the top surface.
physical_description.weight_description: Remarkably light — feels almost insubstantial in the palm, belying its sophisticated internals. Balanced for throwing or placement without fatigue.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer composite frame with embedded graphene heat-dissipation matrix. Optical crown machined from synthetic sapphire.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal polymer body with brushed titanium accent ring around the lens assembly. Anti-reflective coating on optics creates a faint purple-tinted sheen under direct light.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary with brushed silver accent ring. Lens crown appears deep indigo under illumination.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer with subtle radial grip channels molded into the sides for secure single-hand throws. Cool to the touch.
distinctive_features: Concentric lens array with 7 micro-emitter nodes arranged in circular pattern
Central sapphire optic dome with faint internal glow during operation
Recessed power indicator — single RGB status LED barely visible at 2 o'clock position
Thermal vent micro-slots along the bottom rim (thermal signature simulation heat dissipation)
Barely-visible acoustic speaker grille on underside
Proprietary quick-deploy attachment lug at base for drone integration
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: STERLING-NAKAMURA logo (interlocking S-N monogram) laser-etched on one side of the accent ring. Tiny serial plate (2mm × 4mm) mounted below the power indicator. Minimal text — just model 'HDP-3' and manufacture date code.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show subtle wear — minor scuff marks on the grip channels, faint burn marks around the thermal vents from repeated deployment cycles, occasional discoloration of the polymer from dust and thermal cycling. Lenses remain pristine (sapphire is scratch-resistant).
